newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus shares settle after cement-inspired buys.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus shares settle after cement-inspired buys.

text.p: Trading in two Cypriot cement companies was still barred on the Cyprus bourse on Friday as the market remained static, with stocks gaining 0.35 percent over last week, traders said.

The Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) board of directors on Tuesday temporarily suspended trading in shares of Vassiliko Cement and the Cyprus Cement Company amid confusing reports of a takeover or a merger.
"Apart from the Vassiliko - Cyprus Cement story there was no other news to excite the market," said the Cyprus Investment and Securities Corporation (CISCO) in its weekly report.
The CSE index closed at 78.44 points on Friday compared to 78.16 last week, when the bourse saw weekly gains of 2.77 percent because of speculative buying in shares of both cement companies.
"The suspension remains until further notice," bourse director Nondas Metaxas told Reuters on Friday. "The matter is being closely followed by the CSE."
But he indicated more clarifications concerning the intentions of both companies were expected.
Italy's Italcementi ITAI.MA owns 33 percent of Vassiliko and is the biggest shareholder. The Church-controlled Hellenic Mining Company (HMC) is the second largest.

A bull run started on the shares of Vassiliko and Cyprus Cement last week after the head of the Greek Orthodox Church of Cyprus, Archbishop Chrysostomos, told reporters the HMC was interested in selling about 30 percent of Vassiliko shares to the "Cypriot company", referring to Cyprus Cement.
Stavros Galatariotis, chairman of Cyprus Cement, has confirmed he is interested in purchasing a 47 percent-plus stake in Vassiliko, which has an estimated 55 percent share in the local market.
Italcementi has stated it will exercise its preemption right on shares if attempts are made by "third parties" to buy Vassiliko shares controlled by the HMC.
Insurance shares closed at 59.88, up on last week's close of 57.44. Manufacturing stocks closed at 83.21, a marginal drop from 83.22 last week.
